prompt:
You are a grounded brand-outreach assistant for our team. Use only the evidence passages below.
Never use outside knowledge. Return valid JSON only.

Separate three things:
1. OBSERVED FACTS - things a passage actually states about this company. Each fact is a claim with an id (C1, C2, ...),
   the passage id(s) that support it, and an exact quote copied word-for-word from that passage.
2. UNKNOWNS - things the evidence does not tell us (put them in "unknowns"). A channel, program or audience that does
   not appear in these passages is UNKNOWN. It is never a weakness, never a "gap", and never a reason for outreach.
3. PROPOSALS - collaboration ideas from our team. Proposals are not facts, but each must build on a positively supported
   fact (an existing campaign, partnership, product, community, value or theme) and cite that premise.

Rules:
- Put a claim marker like {C1} (curly braces) right after every factual statement in every field, including the
  email and Instagram idea. Do not write citation numbers yourself; markers are converted to citations later.
- A claim's "quote" must be copied character-for-character from the cited passage: 5 to 25 consecutive words, no
  paraphrasing, no joining of separate sentences. If you cannot find such a quote, drop the claim and every sentence
  that depends on it.
- Audience and strategy sentences are factual: each needs a marker. If no passage states the audience, write
  INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of guessing.
- Pitch lines (email subject, hook, concept) should describe the proposed post ("A carousel featuring ...",
  "Collaborate on ..."). Any statement in them about what the company already does needs a marker.
- Respect passage types. "proposed_or_mock_work" and "author_recommendation" passages describe ideas, not things the
  company did: never state them as company activity. "provider_reported_result" passages are claims by a vendor or
  agency: attribute them ("X reports that ..."). "creator_or_influencer_audience_data" describes creators' followers,
  not the company's customers. "vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics" passages are a tool vendor's estimates
  (e.g. inferred age ranges): attribute them and never present them as the company's own data.
  "forward_looking_statement" passages describe plans or intentions, not completed activity.
- Mind time: if a passage describes past activity, do not present it as current.
- "marketing_gaps" may only contain a weakness that a passage positively states. Usually it is [].
- Never promise results. Describe benefits as goals or possibilities ("could", "aims to"), not guaranteed outcomes.
- Decision: write "draft" when at least one concrete, evidence-supported collaboration opportunity exists. Otherwise write
  "abstain", give an abstain_reason, set pitch fields to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and leave collaboration_opportunities empty.
- The email is from our team to the company, proposing one collaborative Instagram post. The pitch, the post idea and
  every collaboration opportunity are for Instagram only (no TikTok, YouTube, podcasts or other channels).
- When a sentence uses a vendor, agency or analytics passage, name that source in the sentence itself
  ("According to AdLibrary, ...", "Attentive reports that ...").
- Each "unknowns" item names one specific thing the passages do not tell us (e.g. "Whether X runs a creator program").
  Never write placeholder text such as "what the evidence does not show".

Required JSON:
{
  "decision": "draft" or "abstain",
  "abstain_reason": "string or empty",
  "claims": [{"id": "C1", "kind": "fact | provider_reported | premise", "statement": "string",
              "passage_ids": ["P1"], "quote": "exact words from the passage"}],
  "brand_summary": "Full sentences, each followed by its marker, e.g. "X makes ... {C1}." Never only markers. Or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "likely_target_audience": "A full sentence followed by its marker, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "current_marketing_strategy": ["text with markers"],
  "unknowns": ["one specific open question, e.g. Whether the company works with creators"],
  "marketing_gaps": [],
  "collaboration_opportunities": ["proposal that builds on a cited fact {C2}"],
  "instagram_post_idea": {"hook": "string", "concept": "string", "why_it_fits": "string"},
  "email_subject": "string",
  "email_body": "string"
}

Company: Coterie (company_id coterie; category: premium baby diapers)
Official domains: coterie.com
Recipient: the marketing team
Packet status: ok

Evidence passages:
[P1] source: https://www.coterie.com/about-us | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Over 2 million diapering essentials donated Supporting families is our reason for being, starting with our own team and extended to our community."

[P2] source: https://www.coterie.com/about-us | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Parents, this one’s for you Before launching any product or service, we ask ourselves, ”Will this make parents’ lives easier?” Your thoughts, opinions, and feedback, help us answer this—so we’re always standing by at hello@coterie.com Two dads are playing with their child who is laying on a yellow blanket.Two dads are playing with their child who is laying on a yellow blanket.Two dads are playing with their child who is laying on a yellow blanket.Two dads are playing with their child who is laying on a yellow blanket."

[P3] source: https://advertising.amazon.com/library/case-studies/envision-horizons-coterie-audience-growth | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"The brand was spending broadly on unqualified audiences while missing shoppers actively seeking solutions for specific needs—sensitive skin, overnight protection, and newborn care—that represented Coterie’s greatest growth opportunity. Coterie partnered with Envision Horizons, an Amazon Ads advanced partner that helps brands build awareness and gain market share through Amazon's advertising capabilities, to rebuild the entire audience strategy. The objective was clear: reach parents actively seeking a premium alternative who, once acquired, would become repeat buyers rather than one-time purchasers."

[P4] source: https://online-queso.com/blogs/news/coterie-success-story-frank-yu-premium-diaper-brand | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Frank Yu’s Vision: Finding Opportunity in a Mature Market Coterie and Frank Yu Before launching Coterie, Frank Yu studied how successful consumer brands built loyalty. He understood that great companies do not only sell products. They sell trust, identity, and a feeling that connects with customers. When Yu examined the diaper market, he saw a category that was massive but surprisingly predictable. The biggest brands had strong distribution, decades of history, and loyal customers. However, much of the marketing looked nearly identical. Packages were filled with bright colors and playful characters, while messaging focused mainly on babies."

[P5] source: https://advertising.amazon.com/library/case-studies/envision-horizons-coterie-audience-growth | document: third_party_confirmed | type: provider_reported_result | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Goals Coterie, a premium baby care brand, had established strong brand awareness on Amazon but faced a fundamental audience challenge. Despite meaningful investment in advertising, the brand’s account structure was not built to reach the high-intent parent segments most likely to convert and become loyal customers. An account audit revealed the scope of the opportunity. Approximately 39% of ad spend was not generating sales, 37% of the budget was flowing into broad automatic campaigns, and 59% of campaigns were focused on a competitor strategy that was not converting."

[P6] source: https://advertising.amazon.com/library/case-studies/envision-horizons-coterie-audience-growth | document: third_party_confirmed | type: provider_reported_result | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Envision Horizons layered in Amazon DSP to extend the audience strategy beyond search with three tactics: view remarketing to reconnect with shoppers who had engaged but not converted, lapsed purchase remarketing to re-engage previous buyers, and cross-sell campaigns to introduce existing diaper customers to Coterie’s skincare line. At just 5.2% of total budget, Amazon DSP delivered outsized impact by maintaining connections with high-value audiences across their full purchase journey. A simultaneous Brand Store rebuild ensured that when new audiences arrived, they encountered a premium experience reinforcing Coterie’s value proposition."

[P7] source: https://online-queso.com/blogs/news/coterie-success-story-frank-yu-premium-diaper-brand | document: third_party_confirmed | type: historical_activity | dates in text: 2019 | published: unknown
"Launching Coterie: Reinventing the Diaper Category Coterie The Future of Premium Baby Products When Coterie launched in 2019, it entered a market dominated by some of the largest consumer companies in the world. Instead of competing by copying traditional diaper brands, the company did the opposite. It removed the noise. Coterie introduced minimalist packaging, clean typography, and a modern visual identity. The brand looked less like a traditional baby product and more like a premium skincare or wellness company. This was not simply a design choice. It was a strategic decision. Coterie understood that consumers do not only purchase products based on function."

[P8] source: https://online-queso.com/blogs/news/coterie-success-story-frank-yu-premium-diaper-brand | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Introduction: The Diaper Brand That Changed an Entire Industry The Coterie success story is not about creating a completely new product. It is about seeing an old product in a completely new way. For decades, the diaper industry followed the same formula. Bright colors. Cartoon characters. Loud packaging. Marketing campaigns designed around babies. But there was one major problem: babies were never the ones making the purchase decisions. Parents were. Every year, millions of parents spend thousands of dollars buying diapers, yet many brands continue speaking to them as if they were shopping for children rather than making an important decision for their families."

[P9] source: https://www.coterie.com/about-us | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Free shipping when you bundle. 10% off every Auto Renew order. Free shipping when you bundle. 10% off every Auto Renew order. Free shipping when you bundle. 10% off every Auto Renew order. Free shipping when you bundle."
